_note: Deterministic detection lexicon for the court_language_review MCP tool and its CLI twin. Every pattern is a JavaScript-regex source string, matched case-insensitively. The REWRITE itself is done by the calling model following references/court-language/SKILL.md + TEMPLATES.md + EXAMPLES.md — this file only guarantees nothing banned survives undetected. Severities: stop (do not file/send until rewritten — child-protection, recording admissions, banned clinical labels, threats, profanity), fix (specific, correctable — replace with dated/observable fact), soften (weakens tone/credibility but is not a safety issue).

entries.why: Pleaded clinical/diagnostic labels are banned as claims (GUARDRAILS.md S2: narcissist, alienator, PAS, and coercive control are named explicitly). A diagnosis is not yours to make, and the label becomes the subject of the hearing instead of the conduct.
entries.rewrite_pattern: Replace the label with: the specific behavior + the date(s) it happened + its observed effect on you or the child. Let the court draw the conclusion the label was trying to assert.
entries.example_before: He is a narcissist and an alcoholic who gaslights me constantly.
entries.example_after: On 3/15/24 and 4/2/24, he raised his voice and told me events I documented at the time did not happen. On both dates I could smell alcohol on his breath at pickup.

entries.pattern: \b(always|never|constantly|every (?:single )?time|every time|refuses to ever|without exception|all the time)\b
entries.why: An absolute claim is easy to disprove with one counterexample and invites cross-examination on the word, not the conduct. Courts credit specific, countable incidents.
entries.rewrite_pattern: Replace the absolute with a specific count and the dates: "on N occasions between [date] and [date]" or list the dates.
entries.example_before: He always shows up late and never calls ahead.
entries.example_after: He arrived more than 20 minutes late for pickup on 1/12/24, 2/3/24, and 2/28/24, and did not call ahead on any of those three occasions.

entries.pattern: \b(she wants to|he wants to|she did it to|he did it to|on purpose|deliberately|intentionally|knows that|trying to hurt|trying to punish)\b
entries.why: Motive and intent are conclusions a court draws from conduct, not facts a witness can personally know. Asserting the other party's state of mind is speculation dressed as fact.
entries.rewrite_pattern: Remove the motive claim; state only the observable act and let the pattern (dates, repetition) imply intent if the record supports it.
entries.example_before: She scheduled the appointment during my parenting time on purpose to sabotage my time with our son.
entries.example_after: The appointment was scheduled for 4:00 PM on 6/10/24, during my scheduled parenting time of 3:00-7:00 PM under the current order.

entries.why: A character label is an argument, not evidence, and reads as an attack rather than a fact. It also risks becoming the thing the court scrutinizes about the person who wrote it.
entries.rewrite_pattern: Replace the label with what happened: the specific statement or action, the date, and why it matters to the issue before the court.
entries.example_before: She is manipulative and an unfit parent.
entries.example_after: On 5/1/24, she told the school our son could not be picked up by me despite the current order granting me that day; the school called me directly to confirm.

entries.why: Intensifiers read as editorializing rather than fact, and can make a filing sound less credible even when the underlying fact is accurate.
entries.rewrite_pattern: Delete the intensifier; state the fact plainly and let the fact carry its own weight.
entries.example_before: It is obviously outrageous that he missed the exchange again.
entries.example_after: He did not appear for the exchange scheduled at 5:00 PM on 7/4/24.

entries.why: Profanity and insults have no place in a court filing, testimony, or a message to the other parent, and can be used against the writer as evidence of tone or conduct.
entries.rewrite_pattern: Remove the language entirely; state the underlying fact in neutral, professional terms.
entries.example_before: He is a stupid idiot for missing the appointment again, damn it.
entries.example_after: He did not attend the scheduled 6/1/24 appointment.

entries.pattern: \b(or else|you('|')ll regret|i('|')ll make sure|i will make you pay|you('|')re going to be sorry|if you don('|')t .* i('|')ll)\b
entries.why: A threat or ultimatum, in a filing or a message to the other parent, can itself become evidence used against the writer and can escalate conflict the court is trying to reduce.
entries.rewrite_pattern: Remove the threat; state the request or position once, without a consequence attached, in BIFF register (brief, informative, friendly, firm).
entries.example_before: If you don't have him ready by 5, you'll regret it.
entries.example_after: Per the parenting time order, I will arrive for pickup at 5:00 PM.

entries.pattern: \b(my (?:son|daughter|child) (?:said|told me|says|tells me)|told me that (?:he|she|they) (?:said|told)|the kids? will testify|our (?:son|daughter|child) will testify)\b
entries.why: Absolute child-protection rule (GUARDRAILS.md S8): no exercise, template, or filing may use the child as a witness, messenger, or source. What the child said is also hearsay in nearly every posture, and MRE 803A's child-statement exception applies only in criminal/delinquency proceedings.
entries.rewrite_pattern: Remove the child's statement entirely. If the underlying fact matters, establish it through your own personal-knowledge observation, a document, or a properly noticed witness — never through what the child said.
entries.example_before: My son told me that dad left him home alone for three hours on Saturday.
entries.example_after: On Saturday between approximately 2:00 and 5:00 PM, I was unable to reach the household by phone despite three calls, which I logged at the time.

entries.why: Speculation is not evidence and invites an objection ("lack of personal knowledge" or "speculation"). State only what you actually know.
entries.rewrite_pattern: State what you personally observed or know, or omit the sentence if you do not actually know it.
entries.example_before: He probably didn't take him to school again.
entries.example_after: The school's attendance record shows an absence on 3/1/24; I do not have personal knowledge of the reason.

entries.why: These are legal conclusions for the court to reach, not facts a layperson pleads. Asserting the legal label instead of the facts underlying it can read as argument and can overstate what the record actually shows.
entries.rewrite_pattern: Describe the specific facts (what happened, when, how you know) and let the court apply the legal label if warranted; do not assert the legal conclusion yourself.
entries.example_before: This is custodial interference and he should be held in contempt.
entries.example_after: He did not return our son at the 6:00 PM exchange time on 8/1/24 and 8/8/24, as required by the current order.

entries.pattern: \b(i recorded|i taped|i secretly recorded|i tracked (?:her|him|them)|i logged into (?:her|his|their)|i installed (?:a )?(?:tracker|spyware|monitoring app)|i accessed (?:her|his|their) (?:phone|account|email))\b
entries.why: Michigan recording/surveillance law is unsettled and the exposure can be criminal (GUARDRAILS.md S9). An admission of recording, tracking, or unauthorized account access must go to a licensed Michigan attorney before it goes anywhere else — never to a filing or a message.
entries.rewrite_pattern: STOP. Do not include this sentence in any filing, testimony, or message. Consult a licensed Michigan attorney before referencing the recording/tracking/access in any way.
entries.example_before: I recorded the phone call where she admitted it, and I also logged into her email to check.
entries.example_after: [REMOVED — consult a licensed Michigan attorney before referencing any recording or account access in a filing, testimony, or message.]

entries.why: A child's full name, date of birth, or school identifies the child in a filing that may become part of the public record. Redaction is the filer's sole responsibility (MCR 1.109(D)(10)(a)); this project's own rule is stricter than the bare minimum (GUARDRAILS.md S11a).
entries.rewrite_pattern: Replace the child's full name with initials and age; remove the specific school name unless the court has specifically required it, and use a generic descriptor ("the child's school") instead.
entries.example_before: Jane Marie Smith (DOB 4/1/2016) attends Lincoln Elementary School.
entries.example_after: J.M.S. (age 8) attends the child's current elementary school.

affidavit.register: First person, numbered paragraphs, facts within personal knowledge only, no argument.
forbidden: Argument or legal conclusions
Anything not within personal knowledge
Characterizations or clinical labels
Paragraphs longer than roughly 3 sentences
affidavit.rewrite_recipe: One fact per numbered paragraph. State how you know it. Attach any document referenced rather than describing it. Stop before the paragraph becomes argument.

motion_brief.register: Argument allowed, but every factual predicate must be cited to an exhibit or the record.
forbidden: An asserted fact with no exhibit or record cite
Clinical labels or characterizations standing in for a legal standard
Speculation about the other party's motive
motion_brief.rewrite_recipe: For every factual sentence, attach a citation to the exhibit or record that proves it. Keep the characterization-free rule even in argument — argue the standard, not the person.

allowed: A direct answer to the question asked
"I don't know" or "I don't have that information"
forbidden: A narrative answer to a yes/no question
Volunteering facts not asked for
Characterizing the other party while answering
testimony_answer.rewrite_recipe: Answer only what was asked, in one to two sentences. Stop. Do not explain further unless asked to.

message_to_other_parent.register: BIFF: brief, informative, friendly, firm. No history, no accusations.
allowed: The specific logistical fact or request
A firm, single statement of your position
forbidden: A recap of relationship history or past grievances
Accusations or characterizations
Threats, ultimatums, or profanity
More than roughly 2-5 sentences
message_to_other_parent.rewrite_recipe: State the fact. State your position once. End the message. Do not respond to bait in the same message.

allowed: The pattern this incident fits, named neutrally
forbidden: Interpretation presented as fact
Clinical labels
What the child said, presented as your own knowledge
incident_log.rewrite_recipe: Use the FACT structure: Facts (observable only) / Action (what you did) / Context (the pattern) / Time (date, time, location).

objection_to_recommendation.register: Specific finding + why the record does not support it + requested relief.
allowed: A named, specific finding or legal application objected to
A record cite (transcript page or exhibit)
forbidden: A blanket objection to "the entire recommendation"
New facts not in the referee-hearing record without a showing of unavailability
Argument about the other party's character
objection_to_recommendation.rewrite_recipe: One row per objection: the finding (quoted or closely paraphrased), why it is wrong (fact or law), the record cite, and the correction requested.
